What is the last name of the family that these communities have in common?

**Adams** is a city in [Adams County, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams_County,_Wisconsin "Adams County, Wisconsin"), United States. The population was 1,761 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). The city is located within the [Town of Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Adams_County,_Wisconsin "Adams, Adams County, Wisconsin").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Adams was originally called South Friendship, but after a petition from residents who did not like the name, the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway") changed it to Adams due to its short nature.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-5) The town became a division point in 1911 for the lines of the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-books.google.com-6) The Milwaukee, Sparta, and Northwestern Railroad, a subsidiary of the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway"), began the "Air Line" or "Adams Cutoff" from Adams towards [Sparta, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparta,_Wisconsin "Sparta, Wisconsin") in 1910.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-MONROE-7)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Adams had a population of 1,761. The median age was 46.9 years. 20.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 24.2% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 92.9 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 88.1 males age 18 and over.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DP-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020PL-12)

0.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 100.0% lived in rural areas.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DHC-13)

There were 808 households in Adams, of which 21.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 29.0% were married-couple households, 25.4% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 36.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 43.1% of all households were made up of individuals and 20.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DP-11)

There were 917 housing units, of which 11.9% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 3.6% and the rental vacancy rate was 7.7%.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DP-11)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-3) of 2010, there were 1,967 people, 886 households, and 479 families living in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 666.8 inhabitants per square mile (257.5/km 2). There were 990 housing units at an average density of 335.6 per square mile (129.6/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 94.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 1.3% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.9% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.5% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.7% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 1.9% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 2.3% of the population.

There were 886 households, of which 27.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 33.6% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 15.5% had a female householder with no husband present, 5.0% had a male householder with no wife present, and 45.9% were non-families. 41.5% of all households were made up of individuals, and 22.3% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.20 and the average family size was 2.96.

The median age in the city was 42.2 years. 24% of residents were under the age of 18; 7.5% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 21.7% were from 25 to 44; 25.2% were from 45 to 64; and 21.5% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 46.0% male and 54.0% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-GR2-4) of 2000, there were 1,914 people, 769 households, and 470 families living in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 650.1 people per square mile (251.4/km 2). There were 847 housing units at an average density of 287.7 per square mile (111.2/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 97.75% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.16% [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)") or [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.37% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.05% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.47% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 1.20% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 1.93% of the population.

There were 769 households, out of which 31.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 42.1% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 15.0% had a female householder with no husband present, and 38.8% were non-families. 35.0% of all households were made up of individuals, and 17.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.34 and the average family size was 3.00.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 26.1% under the age of 18, 6.9% from 18 to 24, 25.6% from 25 to 44, 18.2% from 45 to 64, and 23.1% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 39 years. For every 100 females, there were 81.4 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 75.9 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $26,250, and the median income for a family was $32,981. Males had a median income of $32,039 versus $20,917 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $14,744. About 9.7% of families and 14.6% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 14.4% of those under age 18 and 15.9% of those age 65 or over.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[Adams County Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams_County_Airport "Adams County Airport") (63C) serves Adams and the surrounding communities. The [Union Pacific Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Pacific_Railroad "Union Pacific Railroad")'s [Adams Subdivision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams_Subdivision "Adams Subdivision"), part of a main rail line between [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee") and the [Twin Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_Cities "Twin Cities"), passes through Adams. There has been no rail passenger service since the end of the _[Twin Cities 400](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin\_Cities\_400 "Twin Cities 400")_ in 1963, which was operated by the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway").

**Adams** is a city in [Adams County, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams_County,_Wisconsin "Adams County, Wisconsin"), United States. The population was 1,761 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). The city is located within the [Town of Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Adams_County,_Wisconsin "Adams, Adams County, Wisconsin").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Adams was originally called South Friendship, but after a petition from residents who did not like the name, the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway") changed it to Adams due to its short nature.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-5) The town became a division point in 1911 for the lines of the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-books.google.com-6) The Milwaukee, Sparta, and Northwestern Railroad, a subsidiary of the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway"), began the "Air Line" or "Adams Cutoff" from Adams towards [Sparta, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparta,_Wisconsin "Sparta, Wisconsin") in 1910.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-MONROE-7)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Adams had a population of 1,761. The median age was 46.9 years. 20.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 24.2% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 92.9 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 88.1 males age 18 and over.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DP-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020PL-12)

0.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 100.0% lived in rural areas.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DHC-13)

There were 808 households in Adams, of which 21.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 29.0% were married-couple households, 25.4% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 36.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 43.1% of all households were made up of individuals and 20.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DP-11)

There were 917 housing units, of which 11.9% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 3.6% and the rental vacancy rate was 7.7%.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-Census2020DP-11)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-3) of 2010, there were 1,967 people, 886 households, and 479 families living in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 666.8 inhabitants per square mile (257.5/km 2). There were 990 housing units at an average density of 335.6 per square mile (129.6/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 94.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 1.3% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.9% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.5% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.7% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 1.9% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 2.3% of the population.

There were 886 households, of which 27.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 33.6% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 15.5% had a female householder with no husband present, 5.0% had a male householder with no wife present, and 45.9% were non-families. 41.5% of all households were made up of individuals, and 22.3% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.20 and the average family size was 2.96.

The median age in the city was 42.2 years. 24% of residents were under the age of 18; 7.5% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 21.7% were from 25 to 44; 25.2% were from 45 to 64; and 21.5% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 46.0% male and 54.0% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Wisconsin#cite_note-GR2-4) of 2000, there were 1,914 people, 769 households, and 470 families living in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 650.1 people per square mile (251.4/km 2). There were 847 housing units at an average density of 287.7 per square mile (111.2/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 97.75% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.16% [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)") or [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.37% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.05% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.47% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 1.20% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 1.93% of the population.

There were 769 households, out of which 31.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 42.1% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 15.0% had a female householder with no husband present, and 38.8% were non-families. 35.0% of all households were made up of individuals, and 17.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.34 and the average family size was 3.00.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 26.1% under the age of 18, 6.9% from 18 to 24, 25.6% from 25 to 44, 18.2% from 45 to 64, and 23.1% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 39 years. For every 100 females, there were 81.4 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 75.9 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $26,250, and the median income for a family was $32,981. Males had a median income of $32,039 versus $20,917 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $14,744. About 9.7% of families and 14.6% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 14.4% of those under age 18 and 15.9% of those age 65 or over.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Wisconsin&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[Adams County Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams_County_Airport "Adams County Airport") (63C) serves Adams and the surrounding communities. The [Union Pacific Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Pacific_Railroad "Union Pacific Railroad")'s [Adams Subdivision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams_Subdivision "Adams Subdivision"), part of a main rail line between [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee") and the [Twin Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin_Cities "Twin Cities"), passes through Adams. There has been no rail passenger service since the end of the _[Twin Cities 400](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twin\_Cities\_400 "Twin Cities 400")_ in 1963, which was operated by the [Chicago and North Western Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_and_North_Western_Railway "Chicago and North Western Railway").

**Adams** is a village in [Gage County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gage_County,_Nebraska "Gage County, Nebraska"), [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska"), United States. The population was 604 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census,_2020 "United States Census, 2020").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The area that would become the village of Adams was initially colonized by the namesake of the settlement, an Indiana pioneer named Tyler Adams (1808–1887).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-4) He arrived in 1857; however, the village of Adams did not exist until John O. Adams negotiated deals with a railroad company that intended to set tracks through his land in 1873.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-5)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the village has a total area of 0.58 square miles (1.50 km 2), all land.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-Gazetteer_files-6) The village lies approximately twenty-five miles south of the state capital city of [Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln,_Nebraska "Lincoln, Nebraska").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-7)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-10) of 2010, there were 573 people, 197 households, and 141 families residing in the village. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 987.9 inhabitants per square mile (381.4/km 2). There were 217 housing units at an average density of 374.1 per square mile (144.4/km 2). The racial makeup of the village was 99.7% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.2% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), and 0.2% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") people of any race were 0.7% of the population.

There were 197 households, of which 38.6% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 53.8% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 11.2% had a female householder with no husband present, 6.6% had a male householder with no wife present, and 28.4% were non-families. 27.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 17.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.37 and the average family size was 2.84.

The median age in the village was 40.8 years. 24.6% of residents were under the age of 18; 9% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 20.5% were from 25 to 44; 17.6% were from 45 to 64; and 28.3% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the village was 49.7% male and 50.3% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-GR2-3) of 2000, there were 489 people, 187 households, and 123 families residing in the village. The population density was 821.8 inhabitants per square mile (317.3/km 2). There were 200 housing units at an average density of 336.1 per square mile (129.8/km 2). The racial makeup of the village was 99.18% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), and 0.82% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") people of any race were 1.23% of the population.

There were 187 households, out of which 31.0% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 55.6% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 6.4% had a female householder with no husband present, and 33.7% were non-families. 32.1% of all households were made up of individuals, and 23.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.25 and the average family size was 2.85.

In the village, the population was spread out, with 21.5% under the age of 18, 4.1% from 18 to 24, 23.9% from 25 to 44, 14.7% from 45 to 64, and 35.8% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 45 years. For every 100 females, there were 76.5 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 73.0 males.

As of 2000 the median income for a household in the village was $35,625, and the median income for a family was $44,792. Males had a median income of $30,139 versus $17,431 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the village was $15,243. About 1.7% of families and 3.0% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including none of those under age 18 and 10.0% of those age 65 or over.

## Religion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Religion")]

The village of Adams has three churches, all with denominations of traditional [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism"). The American Lutheran Church is the only non-[Methodist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodism "Methodism") church within the village's borders.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-choich-11) There is also a chapel in the Gold Crest Retirement Center, which is located within Adams.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-12)

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Culture")]

Two annual festivals occur in Adams. One is centered around [American Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Independence_Day "American Independence Day") celebrations, and incukdes volleyball and softball sporting events, a village-wide [barbecue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbecue "Barbecue"), and a fireworks show; this takes place on the first Saturday of every July. A second event is Adams Community Days, which hosts volleyball, golf, and softball events; another village barbecue; and several tractor pull events.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-13)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Education")]

The village of Adams is home to the offices and facilities of the [Daniel Freeman Public School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Freeman_Public_Schools?action=edit&redlink=1 "Daniel Freeman Public Schools (page does not exist)") district,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-14) a [Class 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_school_districts_in_Nebraska "List of school districts in Nebraska") entity composed of Freeman Elementary School and [Freeman High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeman_High_School_(Adams,_Nebraska)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Freeman High School (Adams, Nebraska) (page does not exist)").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-15) This is one of four school districts serving [Gage County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gage_County,_Nebraska "Gage County, Nebraska").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-16)

## Healthcare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Healthcare")]

The village of Adams is home to the Adams Primary Care Clinic, a satellite of the Saint Elizabeth Physician Network spearheaded by Saint Elizabeth Regional Medical Center in the state capital of [Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln,_Nebraska "Lincoln, Nebraska"). It also houses the Lake Crest Pharmacy, which serves Adams and neighboring communities as well. Offices pertaining to [orthodontics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthodontics "Orthodontics"), [dentistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentistry "Dentistry"), and [optometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optometry "Optometry") are located in the village of Adams, although all three are secondary to the main offices in Lincoln.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-17)

**Adams** is a village in [Gage County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gage_County,_Nebraska "Gage County, Nebraska"), [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska"), United States. The population was 604 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census,_2020 "United States Census, 2020").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The area that would become the village of Adams was initially colonized by the namesake of the settlement, an Indiana pioneer named Tyler Adams (1808–1887).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-4) He arrived in 1857; however, the village of Adams did not exist until John O. Adams negotiated deals with a railroad company that intended to set tracks through his land in 1873.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-5)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the village has a total area of 0.58 square miles (1.50 km 2), all land.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-Gazetteer_files-6) The village lies approximately twenty-five miles south of the state capital city of [Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln,_Nebraska "Lincoln, Nebraska").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-7)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-10) of 2010, there were 573 people, 197 households, and 141 families residing in the village. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 987.9 inhabitants per square mile (381.4/km 2). There were 217 housing units at an average density of 374.1 per square mile (144.4/km 2). The racial makeup of the village was 99.7% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.2% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), and 0.2% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") people of any race were 0.7% of the population.

There were 197 households, of which 38.6% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 53.8% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 11.2% had a female householder with no husband present, 6.6% had a male householder with no wife present, and 28.4% were non-families. 27.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 17.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.37 and the average family size was 2.84.

The median age in the village was 40.8 years. 24.6% of residents were under the age of 18; 9% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 20.5% were from 25 to 44; 17.6% were from 45 to 64; and 28.3% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the village was 49.7% male and 50.3% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-GR2-3) of 2000, there were 489 people, 187 households, and 123 families residing in the village. The population density was 821.8 inhabitants per square mile (317.3/km 2). There were 200 housing units at an average density of 336.1 per square mile (129.8/km 2). The racial makeup of the village was 99.18% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), and 0.82% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") people of any race were 1.23% of the population.

There were 187 households, out of which 31.0% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 55.6% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 6.4% had a female householder with no husband present, and 33.7% were non-families. 32.1% of all households were made up of individuals, and 23.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.25 and the average family size was 2.85.

In the village, the population was spread out, with 21.5% under the age of 18, 4.1% from 18 to 24, 23.9% from 25 to 44, 14.7% from 45 to 64, and 35.8% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 45 years. For every 100 females, there were 76.5 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 73.0 males.

As of 2000 the median income for a household in the village was $35,625, and the median income for a family was $44,792. Males had a median income of $30,139 versus $17,431 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the village was $15,243. About 1.7% of families and 3.0% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including none of those under age 18 and 10.0% of those age 65 or over.

## Religion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Religion")]

The village of Adams has three churches, all with denominations of traditional [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism"). The American Lutheran Church is the only non-[Methodist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodism "Methodism") church within the village's borders.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-choich-11) There is also a chapel in the Gold Crest Retirement Center, which is located within Adams.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-12)

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Culture")]

Two annual festivals occur in Adams. One is centered around [American Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Independence_Day "American Independence Day") celebrations, and incukdes volleyball and softball sporting events, a village-wide [barbecue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbecue "Barbecue"), and a fireworks show; this takes place on the first Saturday of every July. A second event is Adams Community Days, which hosts volleyball, golf, and softball events; another village barbecue; and several tractor pull events.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-13)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Education")]

The village of Adams is home to the offices and facilities of the [Daniel Freeman Public School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Freeman_Public_Schools?action=edit&redlink=1 "Daniel Freeman Public Schools (page does not exist)") district,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-14) a [Class 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_school_districts_in_Nebraska "List of school districts in Nebraska") entity composed of Freeman Elementary School and [Freeman High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeman_High_School_(Adams,_Nebraska)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Freeman High School (Adams, Nebraska) (page does not exist)").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-15) This is one of four school districts serving [Gage County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gage_County,_Nebraska "Gage County, Nebraska").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-16)

## Healthcare

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Nebraska&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Healthcare")]

The village of Adams is home to the Adams Primary Care Clinic, a satellite of the Saint Elizabeth Physician Network spearheaded by Saint Elizabeth Regional Medical Center in the state capital of [Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln,_Nebraska "Lincoln, Nebraska"). It also houses the Lake Crest Pharmacy, which serves Adams and neighboring communities as well. Offices pertaining to [orthodontics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthodontics "Orthodontics"), [dentistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentistry "Dentistry"), and [optometry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optometry "Optometry") are located in the village of Adams, although all three are secondary to the main offices in Lincoln.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Nebraska#cite_note-17)

**Adams** is an [unincorporated community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_area "Unincorporated area") in [Schleicher County, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schleicher_County,_Texas "Schleicher County, Texas"), United States. Its elevation is 2,300 ft (701 m).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Texas#cite_note-1) Adams is located northeast of [Eldorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldorado,_Texas "Eldorado, Texas"), the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of Schleicher County.

## Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Texas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Climate")]

The climate in this area is characterized by hot, humid summers and generally mild to cool winters. According to the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), Adams has a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate"), _Cfa_ on climate maps.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Texas#cite_note-2)

**Adams** is an [unincorporated community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_area "Unincorporated area") in [Schleicher County, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schleicher_County,_Texas "Schleicher County, Texas"), United States. Its elevation is 2,300 ft (701 m).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Texas#cite_note-1) Adams is located northeast of [Eldorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldorado,_Texas "Eldorado, Texas"), the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of Schleicher County.

## Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adams,_Texas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Climate")]

The climate in this area is characterized by hot, humid summers and generally mild to cool winters. According to the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), Adams has a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate"), _Cfa_ on climate maps.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams,_Texas#cite_note-2)

**Grand Junction** is a [home rule municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Colorado#Home_rule_municipality "List of municipalities in Colorado") that is the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of and the largest city in [Mesa County, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesa_County,_Colorado "Mesa County, Colorado"), United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-COMun-1) Grand Junction's population was 65,560 at the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), making it the most populous city in western Colorado and the [17th most populous Colorado municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Colorado#Municipalities "List of municipalities in Colorado") overall.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-2020_Census-4)

As western Colorado's largest city, Grand Junction is the economic and cultural center of the [Western Slope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Western_Slope "Colorado Western Slope") region. The city is a transportation hub, situated at the convergence of [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70 "Interstate 70"), [U.S. Highway 50](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Highway_50 "U.S. Highway 50") and [U.S. Highway 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Highway_6 "U.S. Highway 6"). Grand Junction is also home to [Colorado Mesa University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Mesa_University "Colorado Mesa University"), enrolling nearly 10,000 students annually.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-7)

The city is the anchor of the [Grand Junction metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesa_County "Mesa County"), home to over 162,000 residents as of 2025. It is located in the heart of the [Grand Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Valley_(Colorado-Utah) "Grand Valley (Colorado-Utah)"), a large Colorado River valley stretching over 30 miles (48 km) east-to-west and 5 miles (8.0 km) north-to-south. Grand Junction comprises the largest urban center between [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver") and [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"), as well as the most densely populated area and the only metropolitan area in Colorado outside of the [Front Range Urban Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range_Urban_Corridor "Front Range Urban Corridor").

## Description

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Description")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Confluence_of_the_Gunnison_and_Colorado_rivers.JPG/250px-Confluence_of_the_Gunnison_and_Colorado_rivers.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Confluence_of_the_Gunnison_and_Colorado_rivers.JPG)

The junction of the [Gunnison River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnison_River "Gunnison River") (foreground) and [Colorado River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_River "Colorado River"), historically known as the Grand River

Grand Junction is 247 miles (398 km) west-southwest of the [Colorado State Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_State_Capitol "Colorado State Capitol") in [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"). The city has a [council–manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council%E2%80%93manager_government "Council–manager government") form of government.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-GR6-8) It is a major commercial and transportation hub within the large area between the [Green River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_River_(Colorado_River) "Green River (Colorado River)") and the [Continental Divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Divide_of_the_Americas "Continental Divide of the Americas"), and the largest city in Colorado outside of the [Front Range Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range_urban_corridor "Front Range urban corridor").

The city is along the [Colorado River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_River_(U.S.) "Colorado River (U.S.)"), at its confluence with the [Gunnison River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnison_River "Gunnison River"), which comes in from the south. "Grand" refers to the historical Grand River, renamed the Upper Colorado River in 1921. "Junction" refers to the confluence of the Colorado and Gunnison rivers. Grand Junction has been nicknamed "River City". It is near the midpoint of a 30-mile (48 km) arcing valley, known as the [Grand Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Valley_(Colorado-Utah) "Grand Valley (Colorado-Utah)"); since the late 19th century it has been a major [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit "Fruit")-growing region. The valley was long occupied by the [Ute people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ute_people "Ute people") and earlier indigenous cultures. It was not settled by European-American farmers until the 1880s. Since the late 20th century, several [wineries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winery "Winery") have been established in the area.

The [Colorado National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_National_Monument "Colorado National Monument"), a unique series of canyons and mesas, overlooks the city on the west. Most of the area is surrounded by federal public lands managed by the US [Bureau of Land Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Land_Management "Bureau of Land Management"). [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_in_Colorado "Interstate 70 in Colorado") connects the city eastward to [Glenwood Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenwood_Springs,_Colorado "Glenwood Springs, Colorado") and [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver") and westward to [Green River, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_River,_Utah "Green River, Utah"); [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City") is reached to the west via [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_in_Utah "Interstate 70 in Utah") and [U.S Route 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_6_in_Utah "U.S. Route 6 in Utah"), and [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas") via [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_in_Utah "Interstate 70 in Utah") and [Interstate 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_15_in_Utah "Interstate 15 in Utah").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

In September 1881, the former [Ute Indian Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ute_people#Ute_ancestral_lands_and_culture "Ute people") was abolished and the Utes were forced into a reservation so that the U.S. government could open the area to settlers. [Clinton County, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_County,_Pennsylvania "Clinton County, Pennsylvania")-born [George Addison Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_A._Crawford "George A. Crawford") (1827–91) soon purchased a plot of land.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-9) On July 22, 1882, he incorporated the town of Grand Junction and planted [Colorado's first vineyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_wine "Colorado wine") near [Palisade, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palisade,_Colorado "Palisade, Colorado"), causing the area to become known as the Colorado Wine Country.

Grand Junction also has a storied past with gunfighters, miners, and early settlers of the American Southwest. Prior to its incorporation as the city of Grand Junction, the community was known as **Ute**, and was also briefly called **West Denver**.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The [narrow gauge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrow_gauge "Narrow gauge")[Denver and Rio Grande Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_and_Rio_Grande_Railroad "Denver and Rio Grande Railroad") reached Grand Junction from the southeast, from [Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo,_Colorado "Pueblo, Colorado") via [Gunnison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunnison,_Colorado "Gunnison, Colorado") in 1882, followed in 1890 by the [standard gauge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_gauge "Standard gauge") Rio Grande Junction Railway from the northeast, from [New Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Castle,_Colorado "New Castle, Colorado") (jointly owned by the D&RG and the [Colorado Midland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Midland "Colorado Midland")).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-Beebe_1962-10) These greatly contributed to the expansion and settlement of the area.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

At the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the city had a total area of 25,649 acres (103.799 km 2) (40.077 sq mi), including 283 acres (1.147 km 2) (.443 sq mi) of water.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-2020_Census-4)

## Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Climate")]

Grand Junction has a [cold semi-arid climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_semi-arid_climate "Cold semi-arid climate") ([Köppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"): _BSk_). It sits in a large area of [high desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Plateau "Colorado Plateau") lands in Western Colorado. Winters are cold and dry, with a January mean temperature of 27.4°F (−2.6°C). Due to its location _west_ of the Rockies, Grand Junction does not receive as much influence from the [Chinook winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_wind "Chinook wind") as locations in Colorado east of the [Front Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range "Front Range"), yet it does receive protection from the Arctic air masses that can settle to the east of the Rockies. This is illustrated by the fact that from December to February, highs reach 50°F (10°C) only 18 days.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-NOAA-G-11) Lows drop to 0°F (−17.8°C) or below on 2.9 nights per year.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-NOAA-G-11) Snowfall is low compared to much of the rest of the state, averaging 17.6 inches (45 cm) per season; only once in the entire period of record dating to 1893, has observed 10 inches (25 cm) in a calendar day, though the median is 6.3 inches (16.0 cm), and moreover, snow cover is intermittent.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-NOAA-G-11) Snow is greatest in December and January. Spring warming is gradual but quickens when nearing June; the average last freeze date is April 25. Summer is hot and dry, with a July mean temperature of 78.2°F (25.7°C). Grand Junction averages 68 days a year with temperatures at 90°F (32°C) or above, and an average 8 days attaining 100°F (38°C) or more. Autumn cooling is rapid, with the average first freeze date being October 11. The area receives little precipitation year-round, averaging 9.05 inches (229.9 mm), with no real seasonal spike. Sunshine hours are abundant, even in winter, and total just over 3,200 hours per year, or 73% of the possible total.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-HKO-12)

Grand Junction is the principal city of the [Grand Junction, CO Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_CO_Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "Grand Junction, CO Metropolitan Statistical Area").

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Grand Junction had a population of 65,560. The median age was 39.1 years. 18.8% of residents were under the age of 18 and 20.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 97.5 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 95.4 males age 18 and over.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-Census2020DP-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-Census2020PL-18)

99.6% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.4% lived in rural areas.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-Census2020DHC-19)

There were 27,584 households in Grand Junction, of which 23.9% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 42.3% were married-couple households, 21.3% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 29.2% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 33.7% of all households were made up of individuals and 15.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-Census2020DP-17)

There were 29,431 housing units, of which 6.3% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.7% and the rental vacancy rate was 6.8%.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-Census2020DP-17)

As of the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census"), there were 41,986 people, 17,865 households, and 10,540 families residing in the city. The population density was 1,362.6 inhabitants per square mile (526.1/km 2). There were 18,784 housing units at an average density of 609.6 per square mile (235.4/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 91.78% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.60% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.94% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.76% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.12% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), 3.81% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 1.99% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") residents of any race were 10.86% of the population.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-GR2-20)

There were 17,865 households, out of which 25.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 46.1% were married couples living together, 9.4% had a female householder with no husband present, and 41.0% were non-families. Of all households 33.2% were made up of individuals, and 13.8% had one living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.23 and the average family size was 2.84.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-GR2-20)

In the city, 21.2% of the population was under the age of 18, 11.9% was from 18 to 24, 26.3% from 25 to 44, 22.8% from 45 to 64, and 17.9% was 65 years of age or older. The median age was 39 years. For every 100 females, there were 95.1 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 92.6 males.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-GR2-20)

The population figures are for Grand Junction only; the city abuts smaller towns and unincorporated county areas which contribute to area commerce.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-GR2-20)

The median income for a household in the city was $33,152, and the median income for a family was $43,851. Males had a median income of $31,685 versus $22,804 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $19,692. About 7.5% of families and 11.9% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 11.8% of those under age 18 and 9.0% of those age 65 or over.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-GR2-20)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Economy")]

### Economic history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Economic history")]

From the time settlers arrived in the 1880s until the 1960s, three of the main economic activities in the region were farming, fruit growing, and cattle raising.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Fruit orchards, particularly between Grand Junction and Palisade to the east, remain important to the region's reputation and economy to the present day. Fruits most often grown are peaches, pears, apricots, plums, cherries, and, particularly since the 1980s, grapes for wine. In this semi-arid environment, these orchards thrive from a combination of abundant sunshine and irrigation from a system of canals that divert water from the Colorado River.

Attempts were made to establish sugar beet farming and beet sugar production. The Grand Valley Sugar Company established a campaign in 1893, sending three train carloads to the [Utah-Idaho Sugar Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah-Idaho_Sugar_Company "Utah-Idaho Sugar Company"). Several tariffs and subsidies to domestic sugar were established in the 1890s, which led to uncertainty in the market. After the 1897 [Dingley Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingley_Act "Dingley Act"), the company was revived in 1898 and rallied to build a sugar factory. They failed to fundraise to build the plant. At the same time, Charles N. Cox was able to organize an effort to establish a factory in 1898. [John F. Campion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Campion "John F. Campion") and others, including [James Joseph Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Joseph_Brown "James Joseph Brown"), [Eben Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eben_Smith "Eben Smith"), Charles E. Mitchell, George Trimble, James R. McKinnie, and [Charles Boettcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Boettcher "Charles Boettcher") invested, creating the Colorado Sugar Manufacturing Company in 1899 and contracting [E. H. Dyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._H._Dyer "E. H. Dyer") to build a factory. After they failed, they sold the plant to local investors, who were able to make it a success. The Campion-Boettcher group then created the [Great Western Sugar Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Western_Sugar_Company "Great Western Sugar Company").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-silverwedge-21)

Grand Junction was home to the [Climax Uranium Mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climax_Uranium_Mill "Climax Uranium Mill"), a now decommissioned mill that provided uranium ore to the [US Atomic Energy Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Atomic_Energy_Commission "US Atomic Energy Commission"). It produced 2.2 million tons of [uranium tailings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium_tailings "Uranium tailings"), a by product of uranium mining which can be unsafe. For decades, Grand Junction residents were able to collect as much of the fine radioactive gray sand as they wanted for free. It was used as construction material all over town.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-23)

Education and healthcare have been important to the economy of the area, especially since the 1950s, with the rise of [Colorado Mesa University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Mesa_University "Colorado Mesa University") and St. Mary's Hospital as leading employers in these fields.

Vast [oil shale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_shale "Oil shale") reserves were known to exist near [Parachute, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parachute,_Colorado "Parachute, Colorado"), in the [Piceance Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piceance_Basin "Piceance Basin"). The oil embargoes of the 1970s and high gas prices resulted in major financial interest in the region. Exxon purchased rights and used Grand Junction as its seat of operations. The city and the surrounding [Grand Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Valley_(Colorado-Utah) "Grand Valley (Colorado-Utah)") became prosperous in the 1970s and early 1980s largely because of the effects of [oil shale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_shale "Oil shale") development. The United States, western Colorado in particular, has the largest-known concentration of oil shale in the world (according to the Bureau of Land Management) and holds an estimated 800 gigabarrels of recoverable oil, enough to meet U.S. demand for oil at current levels for 110 years. Known as the "Rock That Burns", the shale can be mined and processed to produce oil. In the past, it was significantly more expensive than conventional oil. Sustained prices above $95 per barrel, however, may make extraction economically attractive in the coming years (see [Oil shale economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_shale_economics "Oil shale economics")). ExxonMobil pulled out of the region because of lower oil prices, which led to economic hardship in the region.

The economic bust, known as "Black Sunday" (May 2, 1982) to the locals, started with a phone call from the president of Exxon to Governor [Richard Douglas Lamm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Douglas_Lamm "Richard Douglas Lamm"), stating that Exxon would cut its losses while retaining mining rights to the (then and currently) uneconomic oil. The economic bust was felt statewide, as Exxon had invested more than US$5 billion in the state. Colorado historian [Tom Noel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Noel_(historian) "Thomas Noel (historian)") observed, "I think that was a definite turning point, and it was a reminder that we were a boom-and-bust state ... There were parallels to the silver crash of 1893."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-24)

By 2008, the economy of Grand Junction appeared to be more diverse and stable than it had been in previous decades. Major contributors to the economy were health care, tourism, agriculture, livestock, and energy mining (gas and oil). Major energy companies had once again invested large amounts of money due to increases in oil and natural gas prices (such as in the years 2005–2008). However, a major drop (in the summer of 2008) of market [natural gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_gas "Natural gas") prices led to reduced gas well drilling and related capital expenditures in the area, significantly slowing the Grand Junction economy in 2009. Reports given in 2009 suggested that Grand Junction had once again been hard-hit economically, with one report by April 2010 listing the area as having had the largest percentage drop in employment of any "small city" in the entire United States.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-25)

By 2008, Grand Junction was being discovered by the "nation's elite business and leisure travelers" as a destination for private jet travel, with nearby [Powderhorn Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powderhorn_Resort "Powderhorn Resort") and other ski resorts proving major attractions.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-26)

## Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Sports")]

Grand Junction's [Colorado National Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_National_Monument "Colorado National Monument") was home to a stage in the [Coors Classic bicycle race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coors_Classic "Coors Classic") known as "The Tour of the Moon" due to the Monument's unique landscape.

Since 1958, the [JUCO World Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JUCO_World_Series "JUCO World Series")[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-28) has been played at [Suplizio Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suplizio_Field "Suplizio Field"). The city is also home to a [Minor League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_League_Baseball "Minor League Baseball") team, the Grand Junction Razorback Suckers, who play in the [Pecos League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecos_League "Pecos League").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-29) Until 2026, Grand Junction was home to the [Grand Junction Jackalopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction_Jackalopes "Grand Junction Jackalopes"), who played in the [Pioneer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pioneer_Baseball_League "Pioneer Baseball League"). The Jackalopes were formerly known as the Grand Junction Rockies, playing as a minor-league affiliate of the [Colorado Rockies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rockies "Colorado Rockies") until becoming independent in 2020. In September 2025, the Jackalopes announced that they would relocate from Grand Junction to a new city.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-30)

Grand Junction is also home to a minor league hockey team, the [Grand Junction River Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction_River_Hawks "Grand Junction River Hawks"). The River Hawks compete in the [North American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Hockey_League "North American Hockey League"), and play their home games at River City Sportsplex in Grand Junction.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-31)

Both Suplizio Field and Stocker Stadium also host Colorado Mesa University athletic events, as well as School District 51 sporting events. Stocker Stadium serves as the home football field for the [Colorado Mesa Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Mesa_Mavericks "Colorado Mesa Mavericks"), as well as [Grand Junction High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction_High_School "Grand Junction High School"), [Central High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_High_School_(Grand_Junction,_Colorado) "Central High School (Grand Junction, Colorado)"), [Fruita Monument High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruita_Monument_High_School "Fruita Monument High School"), and [Palisade High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palisade_High_School "Palisade High School").

## Parks and recreation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Parks and recreation")]

The Grand Junction area has developed as a [mountain biking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_biking "Mountain biking") destination, with many bikers coming from the [Front Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range_Urban_Corridor "Front Range Urban Corridor") of Colorado, the [Salt Lake City area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City_metropolitan_area "Salt Lake City metropolitan area"), and as far away as [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") to enjoy the area's abundant single-track trails. Two prominent trails are the Tabeguache and [Kokopelli trails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kokopelli_trail "Kokopelli trail"), the latter running from near [Loma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loma,_Colorado "Loma, Colorado") to [Moab, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moab,_Utah "Moab, Utah"). [Fruita, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruita,_Colorado "Fruita, Colorado"), with its 18-Road trail system, is within 10 miles of the city and has become a major mountain biking destination.

### K–12

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: K–12")]

The Mesa Valley School District No. 51 provides comprehensive K–12 public education to the Grand Junction area.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-32) School District 51 operates five high schools:

*   [Fruita Monument High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruita_Monument_High_School "Fruita Monument High School")
*   [Grand Junction High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction_High_School "Grand Junction High School")
*   [Central High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_High_School_(Grand_Junction,_Colorado) "Central High School (Grand Junction, Colorado)")
*   [Palisade High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palisade_High_School "Palisade High School")
*   R-5 High School

In addition, the district operates numerous middle, elementary, and other types of schools, including East Middle School, Redlands Middle School, and West Middle School. District 51 partners with [CMU Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMU_Tech "CMU Tech") to operate the Mesa County Career Center, a vocational school owned and operated by Colorado Mesa University. CMU Tech was formerly named Western Colorado Community College.

### Colleges and universities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Colleges and universities")]

Grand Junction is home to two higher education institutions:

*   [Colorado Mesa University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Mesa_University "Colorado Mesa University"), a public university serving nearly 10,000 students. CMU is the largest university in western Colorado. 
    *   Colorado Mesa University also operates [CMU Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMU_Tech "CMU Tech") which specializes in vocational education, offering professional certificates and [Associate of Applied Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associate_of_Applied_Science "Associate of Applied Science") degrees

*   [IntelliTec College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IntelliTec_College "IntelliTec College"), a private for-profit technical college offering professional and vocational certificates.

## Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Media")]

Main article: [Media in Grand Junction, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_in_Grand_Junction,_Colorado "Media in Grand Junction, Colorado")

### Radio

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Radio")]

The Grand Junction [radio market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Media_market "Media market") includes all of [Mesa County, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesa_County,_Colorado "Mesa County, Colorado").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-33) Six AM radio stations and more than 25 FM stations are [licensed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_license "City of license") to broadcast from the city.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-34)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-Locator-35)

### Newspapers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Newspapers")]

Grand Junction is serviced by one local newspaper, the _[Grand Junction Daily Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Junction\_Daily\_Sentinel "Grand Junction Daily Sentinel")_. The Grand Junction area also receives newspaper influence from sources in the greater Denver front range area.

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Television")]

Grand Junction has [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"), and [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") television station affiliates under the call signs of [KJCT-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KJCT-TV "KJCT-TV") (Channel 8), [KKCO-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KKCO-TV "KKCO-TV") (Channel 11), and [KREX-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KREX-TV "KREX-TV") (Channel 5), respectively. Also, Grand Junction has a [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") (Channel 4) affiliate station under the call sign of [KFQX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KFQX "KFQX") that receives news from the Denver FOX affiliate, [KDVR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KDVR "KDVR") (Channel 31) at 9 pm. [KLML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KLML "KLML") (Channel 20) broadcasts [Cozi TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cozi_TV "Cozi TV") programming. KRMJ (Channel 18) is the local PBS affiliate, part of the statewide Rocky Mountain PBS network.

## Infrastructure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]

### Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Amtrak_station_in_Grand_Junction%2C_CO.JPG/250px-Amtrak_station_in_Grand_Junction%2C_CO.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Amtrak_station_in_Grand_Junction,_CO.JPG)

Amtrak station

[Grand Junction Regional Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction_Regional_Airport "Grand Junction Regional Airport") (formerly Walker Field Airport) is the city's major airport. It is the largest in western Colorado and the third-largest in the state behind [Denver International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_International_Airport "Denver International Airport") and [Colorado Springs Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Airport "Colorado Springs Airport"). As of 2026[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Junction,_Colorado&action=edit), it has non-stop flights to [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_International_Airport "Denver International Airport"), [Dallas–Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Fort_Worth_International_Airport "Dallas Fort Worth International Airport"), [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Reid_International_Airport "Harry Reid International Airport"), [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City_International_Airport "Salt Lake City International Airport"), [Phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Sky_Harbor_International_Airport "Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport"), [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_International_Airport "San Francisco International Airport"), and [Santa Ana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne_Airport "John Wayne Airport"), as well as one-stop flights to [Hartford, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_International_Airport "Bradley International Airport"), via Las Vegas.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-36)

The [Central Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Corridor_(Union_Pacific_Railroad) "Central Corridor (Union Pacific Railroad)") line of the [Union Pacific Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Pacific_Railroad "Union Pacific Railroad") goes through Grand Junction. Connecting to Denver and Salt Lake City, it is used by UP and [BNSF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BNSF "BNSF") freight trains as well as the [Amtrak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amtrak "Amtrak")_[California Zephyr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California\_Zephyr "California Zephyr")_, which stops at the [Grand Junction Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction_(Amtrak_station) "Grand Junction (Amtrak station)") on its route between [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Station_(Chicago) "Union Station (Chicago)") and the [San Francisco Bay Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area").

The city is served by [Bustang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bustang "Bustang"), Colorado's state-run intercity bus system, with its West line to Denver and Outrider line to Durango. Local transit is provided by [Grand Valley Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Valley_Transit "Grand Valley Transit") (GVT), which operates 11 bus routes and a "dial-a-ride" service.

The city has a growing network of mixed-use pedestrian and bicycle trails.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-37) The riverfront trail system, which runs next to Colorado River, extends from Loma to Palisade, with missing sections between Las Colonias Park and 29 Rd, and 33 1/2 Rd to 36 1/4 Rd.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-38) The monument trail provides a connection from the riverfront trail and the downtown core to the Lunch Loops. In 2023, the city council passed the pedestrian and bicycle plan, a visionary document to promote better connectivity.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-39) In the same year, the city passed a revised Transportation and Engineering Design Standards (TEDS) to provide clearer guidelines for the development of new bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-40) In 2024, the city was awarded a silver designation by the [League of American Bicyclists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_American_Bicyclists "League of American Bicyclists").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Junction,_Colorado#cite_note-41)
