**Colorado Springs** is a [home rule city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Colorado#Home_rule_municipality "List of municipalities in Colorado") that is the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of and the most populous city in [El Paso County, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso_County,_Colorado "El Paso County, Colorado"), United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-COMun-1) The city had a population of 478,961 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), a 15.02% increase since [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020_Census-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020Pop-11) Colorado Springs is the [second-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Colorado "List of municipalities in Colorado") and [most extensive city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_area "List of United States cities by area") by area in the state of Colorado, and the [40th-most-populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population "List of United States cities by population") in the United States.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-PopEstCities-12) It is the principal city of the [Colorado Springs metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_metropolitan_area "Colorado Springs metropolitan area"), which had 755,105 residents in 2020, and the second-most prominent city of the [Front Range Urban Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range_Urban_Corridor "Front Range Urban Corridor"). It is located in east-central Colorado on [Fountain Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain_Creek_(Arkansas_River_tributary) "Fountain Creek (Arkansas River tributary)"), 70 miles (113 km) south of [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver").

At 6,035 feet (1,839 m),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-gnis-5) the city stands over 1 mile (1.6 km) above sea level. It is near the base of [Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak"), which rises 14,115 feet (4,302.31 m) above sea level on the eastern edge of the [Southern Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rocky_Mountains "Southern Rocky Mountains").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Colorado Springs, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "History of Colorado Springs, Colorado")

For a chronological guide, see [Timeline of Colorado Springs, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "Timeline of Colorado Springs, Colorado").

The [Ute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ute_people "Ute people"), [Arapaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arapaho "Arapaho") and [Cheyenne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne "Cheyenne") peoples were the first recorded inhabiting the area which would become Colorado Springs.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-13) Part of the territory included in the United States' 1803 [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase"), the current city area was designated part of the 1854 [Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Territory "Kansas Territory"). In 1859, after the first local settlement was established, it became part of the [Jefferson Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Territory "Jefferson Territory") on October 24 and of [El Paso County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso_County,_Colorado "El Paso County, Colorado") on November 28. [Colorado City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Colorado_City "Old Colorado City") at the [Front Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range "Front Range") confluence of Fountain and Camp creeks was "formally organized on August 13, 1859"[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-14) during the [Pikes Peak Gold Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak_Gold_Rush "Pikes Peak Gold Rush"). The [Colorado City, Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_City,_Kansas_Territory "Colorado City, Kansas Territory"), post office operated from March 24, 1860, until it closed as the Colorado City, Colorado, post office on June 30, 1917.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-CPO-15) Colorado City served as the capital of the [Colorado Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Territory "Colorado Territory") from November 5, 1861, until August 14, 1862, when the capital was moved to [Golden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden,_Colorado "Golden, Colorado").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-16)

In 1871 the [Colorado Springs Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Company "Colorado Springs Company") laid out the towns of La Font (later called [Manitou Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitou_Springs,_Colorado "Manitou Springs, Colorado")) and **Fountain Colony**, upstream and downstream respectively, of Colorado City.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Harrison-17) Later that year, the Fountain Colony was renamed Colorado Springs.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-18) The Colorado Springs, Colorado Territory, post office opened on December 1, 1871.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-CPO-15) The El Paso County seat shifted from Colorado City in 1873 to the Town of Colorado Springs.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Capace-19) So many immigrants from England had settled in Colorado Springs by the early 1870s that Colorado Springs was locally referred to as "Little London".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-20) The town of Colorado Springs was incorporated on June 19, 1886.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-COMun-1)

A second period of annexations occurred during 1889–90, which included Seavey's Addition, West Colorado Springs, East End, and another [North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_North_End_Historic_District_(Colorado_Springs,_Colorado) "Old North End Historic District (Colorado Springs, Colorado)") addition.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-AnnexXLS1990-21) In 1891 the Broadmoor Land Company built the [Broadmoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadmoor,_Colorado "Broadmoor, Colorado") suburb, which included the [Broadmoor Casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadmoor_Casino "Broadmoor Casino"), and by December 12, 1895, the city had "four Mining Exchanges and 275 mining brokers."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-22) By 1898, the city was designated into quadrants by the north-south Cascade Avenue and the east-west Washington/Pikes Peak avenues.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Directory1898-23):10

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Nikola_Tesla%2C_with_his_equipment_Wellcome_M0014782_-_restoration2.jpg/250px-Nikola_Tesla%2C_with_his_equipment_Wellcome_M0014782_-_restoration2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nikola_Tesla,_with_his_equipment_Wellcome_M0014782_-_restoration2.jpg)

[Nikola Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Tesla "Nikola Tesla") sitting in the Colorado Springs Experimental Station with his "[magnifying transmitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnifying_transmitter "Magnifying transmitter")" generating millions of volts

From 1899 to 1901 [Tesla Experimental Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Experimental_Station "Tesla Experimental Station") operated on Knob Hill,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-24) and aircraft flights to the Broadmoor's neighboring fields began in 1919.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NRHPairport-25)[Alexander Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nichols_Field_(Colorado) "Nichols Field (Colorado)") north of the city opened in 1925, and in 1927 the original [Colorado Springs Municipal Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Municipal_Airport "Colorado Springs Municipal Airport") land was purchased east of the city.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NRHPairport-25)

The city's military presence began during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), beginning with Camp Carson (now the 135,000-acre [Fort Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Carson "Fort Carson") base) that was established in 1941.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26) During the war, the [United States Army Air Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces "United States Army Air Forces") leased land adjacent to the municipal airfield, naming it [Peterson Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Field "Peterson Field") in December 1942.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Prinzo-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Directory1916-28)

In November 1950, [Ent Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ent_Air_Force_Base "Ent Air Force Base") was selected as the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") headquarters for [Air Defense Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Defense_Command "Air Defense Command") (ADC). The former WWII Army Air Base, Peterson Field, which had been inactivated at the end of the war, was re-opened in 1951 as a [U.S. Air Force base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Air_Force_Base "Peterson Air Force Base").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-29)[North American Aerospace Defense Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Aerospace_Defense_Command "North American Aerospace Defense Command") (NORAD) was established as a hardened command and control center within the [Cheyenne Mountain Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Mountain_Complex "Cheyenne Mountain Complex") during the Cold War.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30)

Between 1965 and 1968, the [University of Colorado Colorado Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado_Colorado_Springs "University of Colorado Colorado Springs"), [Pikes Peak State College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak_State_College "Pikes Peak State College") and [Colorado Technical University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Technical_University "Colorado Technical University") were established in or near the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Hellmann-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-32) In 1977 most of the former Ent AFB became a [US Olympic training center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Olympic_Training_Center "United States Olympic Training Center"). The [Libertarian Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)") was founded within the city in the 1970s.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-33)

On October 1, 1981, the Broadmoor Addition,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-AnnexXLS1990-21) Cheyenne Canon, [Ivywild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivywild,_Colorado "Ivywild, Colorado"), Skyway, and Stratton Meadows were annexed after the [Colorado Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Supreme_Court "Colorado Supreme Court") "overturned a district court decision that voided the [annexation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation "Annexation")". Further annexations expanding the city include the Nielson Addition and Vineyard Commerce Park Annexation in September 2008.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-AnnexXLS1990-21)

On June 23, 2012, the [Waldo Canyon fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waldo_Canyon_fire "Waldo Canyon fire") began 4 miles (6.4 km) northwest of the city.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-34) The fire ended up destroying 347 homes and killing two people in the city, causing the evacuation of 32,000 residents.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-35) At the time the fire was the most destructive in state history until it was surpassed by the [Black Forest Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Forest_Fire "Black Forest Fire") the following year.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-36)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Colorado_Springs_CO.jpg/250px-Colorado_Springs_CO.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colorado_Springs_CO.jpg)

View of Colorado Springs and [Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak") from the eastern plains

The city lies in a [semi-arid Steppe region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-skybrary.aero-37) with the [Southern Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rocky_Mountains "Southern Rocky Mountains") to the west, the [Palmer Divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmer_Divide "Palmer Divide") to the north, [high plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains") further east, and high desert lands to the south when leaving [Fountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain,_Colorado "Fountain, Colorado") and approaching [Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo,_Colorado "Pueblo, Colorado").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-SpringsGovInfo-38) Colorado Springs is 69 miles (111 km) or at best one hour and five minutes south of Denver by car using [I-25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_25_in_Colorado "Interstate 25 in Colorado").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-39)

Colorado Springs has the [greatest total area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_area "List of United States cities by area") of any municipality in Colorado. During the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the city had a total area of 195.761 square miles (507.019 km 2) including 0.362 square miles (0.937 km 2) of water.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020_Census-9)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Climate")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/ISS067-E-170859_Colorado_Springs_through_the_clouds.jpg/250px-ISS067-E-170859_Colorado_Springs_through_the_clouds.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ISS067-E-170859_Colorado_Springs_through_the_clouds.jpg)

View of the city through the clouds on July 1, 2022, taken from the International Space Station with north oriented towards the left

Colorado Springs has a cooler, dry-winter [monsoon influenced continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_climate "Continental climate") ([Köppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_Dwa_/_Cwa_), and its location just east of the Rocky Mountains affords it the rapid warming influence from [chinook winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_winds "Chinook winds") during winter but also subjects it to drastic day-to-day variability in weather conditions.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-40) The city has abundant sunshine year-round, averaging 243 sunny days per year,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-42) and receives approximately 16.5 inches (419 mm) of annual [precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology) "Precipitation (meteorology)"). Due to unusually low precipitation for several years after flooding in 1999, Colorado Springs enacted lawn water restrictions in 2002. These were lifted in 2005[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-SpringsGovInfo-38) but permanently reinstated in December 2019.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-43)

Colorado Springs is one of the most active lightning strike areas in the United States.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-skybrary.aero-37) This natural phenomenon led [Nikola Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Tesla "Nikola Tesla") to select Colorado Springs as the preferred location to build his lab and study electricity.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-44)

#### Seasonal climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Seasonal climate")]

December is typically the coldest month, averaging 30.8°F (−0.7°C). Historically, January had been the coldest month, but, in recent years, December has had both lower daily maxima and minima.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-45) Typically, there are 5.2 nights with sub-0°F (−18°C) lows and 23.6 days where the high does not rise above freezing.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NOAA-46)

Snowfall is usually moderate and remains on the ground briefly because of direct sun, with the city receiving 38 inches (97 cm) per season, although the mountains to the west often receive in excess of triple that amount; March is the snowiest month in the region, both by total accumulation and number of days with measurable snowfall. In addition, 8 of the top 10 heaviest 24-hour snowfalls have occurred from March to May.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NOAA-46) Summers are warm, with July, the warmest month, averaging 70.9°F (21.6°C), and 18 days of 90°F (32°C)+ highs annually. Due to the high elevation and aridity, nights are usually relatively cool and rarely does the low remain above 70°F (21°C).[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NOAA-46) Dry weather generally prevails, but brief afternoon thunderstorms are common, especially in July and August when the city receives the majority of its annual rainfall, due to the [North American monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_monsoon "North American monsoon").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-47)

The first autumn freeze and the last freeze in the spring, on average, occur on October 2 and May 6, respectively; the average window for measurable snowfall (≥0.1 in or 0.25 cm) is October 21 through April 25. Extreme temperatures range from 101°F (38°C) on [June 26, 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_North_American_heat_wave "2012 North American heat wave"), and most recently on June 21, 2016, down to −27°F (−33°C) on February 1, 1951, and December 9, 1919.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-48)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population of the city of Colorado Springs was 478,961 ([40th most populous U.S. city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population "List of United States cities by population")), the population of the [Colorado Springs Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "Colorado Springs Metropolitan Statistical Area") was 755,105 ([79th most populous MSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_metropolitan_area "United States metropolitan area")), and the population of the [Front Range Urban Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range_Urban_Corridor "Front Range Urban Corridor") was 5,055,344.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020_Census-9)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [2010 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-59) 78.8% of the population of the city was [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_people "White people") (non-Hispanic Whites were 70.7% of the population,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-60) compared with 86.6% in 1970[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-61)), 16.1% [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") of any race (compared with 7.4% in 1970), 6.3% [Black or African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American "African American"), 3.0% Asian, 1.0% descended from [indigenous peoples of the Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas"), 0.3% descended from [indigenous Hawaiians and other Pacific islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_American "Pacific Islander American"), 5.5% of some other race, and 5.1% of [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_American "Multiracial American"). [Mexican Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_American "Mexican American") made up 14.6% of the city's population, compared with 9.1% in 1990. The median age in the city was 35 years.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-62)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-64)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Economy")]

Colorado Springs's economy is driven primarily by the military, the high-tech industry, and tourism, in that order. The city is experiencing slight growth in the service sectors. As of April 2025, the unemployment rate in Colorado Springs was 4.6%.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-65) The state's unemployment rate was 4.8% compared to 4.2% for the nation.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-66)

### Military

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Military")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/PetersonAFB.jpg/250px-PetersonAFB.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PetersonAFB.jpg)

[United States Space Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Space_Force "United States Space Force")–[Peterson Space Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Space_Force_Base "Peterson Space Force Base") Building 1

As of 2021[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit), there are nearly 45,000 active-duty troops in the Colorado Springs area. There are more than 100,000 veterans and thousands of reservists.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26) The military and defense contractors supply more than 40% of the Pikes Peak region's economy.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26)

Colorado Springs is home to the [Peterson Space Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Space_Force_Base "Peterson Space Force Base"), [Schriever Space Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schriever_Space_Force_Base "Schriever Space Force Base"), [Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Mountain_Space_Force_Station "Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station"), U.S. Space Command, and Space Operations Command—the largest contingent of space service military installations, responsible for intelligence gathering, space operations, and cyber missions.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67)

Peterson Space Force Base is responsible for the [North American Aerospace Defense Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Aerospace_Defense_Command "North American Aerospace Defense Command") (NORAD) and the [United States Northern Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Northern_Command "United States Northern Command") (USNORTHCOM) headquarters,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30) Space Operations Command, and Space Deltas 2, 3, and 7.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67) Located at Peterson is the 302nd Airlift Wing, an Air Force Reserve unit, that transports passengers and cargo and fights wildfires.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67)

Schriever Space Force Base is responsible for Joint Task Force-Space Defense and Space Deltas [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Delta_6 "Space Delta 6"), 8, and 9.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67) The NORAD and USNORTHCOM Alternate Command Center is located at the [Cheyenne Mountain Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Mountain_Complex "Cheyenne Mountain Complex").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30) Within the mountain complex, the Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station has been operated by [Space Operations Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Operations_Command "Space Operations Command").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30) On January 13, 2021, the Air Force announced a new permanent home for Space Command, moving it from Colorado Springs to Huntsville, Alabama in 2026, but the decision could be reversed by Congress.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-68)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-72)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/President_Richard_Nixon_Gives_a_Commencement_Ceremony_Speech_at_Air_Force_Academy_in_Colorado_Springs_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-President_Richard_Nixon_Gives_a_Commencement_Ceremony_Speech_at_Air_Force_Academy_in_Colorado_Springs_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Richard_Nixon_Gives_a_Commencement_Ceremony_Speech_at_Air_Force_Academy_in_Colorado_Springs_(cropped).jpg)

President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") gives a commencement ceremony speech at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, June 4, 1969.

Army divisions are trained and stationed at [Fort Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Carson "Fort Carson"). The [United States Air Force Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force_Academy "United States Air Force Academy") was established after World War II on land donated by the City of Colorado Springs.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26)

### Defense industry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Defense industry")]

The defense industry forms a significant part of the Colorado Springs economy, with some of the city's largest employers being defense contractors.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-73) Some defense corporations have left or downsized city campuses, but slight growth has been recorded. Significant defense corporations in the city include [Northrop Grumman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northrop_Grumman "Northrop Grumman"), [Boeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing "Boeing"), [General Dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics "General Dynamics"), [L3Harris Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L3Harris_Technologies "L3Harris Technologies"), [SAIC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_Applications_International_Corporation "Science Applications International Corporation"), [ITT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITT_Corporation "ITT Corporation"), [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin"), and Bluestaq.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-74)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-75)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-76)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-77) The [Space Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Foundation "Space Foundation") is based in Colorado Springs.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-78)

### High-tech industry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: High-tech industry")]

A large percentage of Colorado Springs's economy is still based on manufacturing [high-tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-tech "High-tech") and complex electronic equipment. The high-tech sector in the Colorado Springs area has decreased its overall presence from 2000 to 2006 (from around 21,000 to around 8,000), with notable reductions in information technology and complex electronic equipment.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-79) Current trends project the high-tech employment ratio will continue to decrease.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-autogenerated1-80)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-81)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-82)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-83)[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_]

High-tech corporations offering fibre-optics to the premises connections within the city include: [Lumen Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumen_Technologies "Lumen Technologies"), [Comcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comcast "Comcast") and other providers as of 2023.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-84)[Hewlett-Packard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard") still has some sales, support, and [SAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storage_area_network "Storage area network") storage engineering center for the computer industry.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-85)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-86)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-87)[Storage Networking Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storage_Networking_Industry_Association "Storage Networking Industry Association") is the home of the SNIA Technology Center.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-88)[Keysight Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keysight_Technologies "Keysight Technologies"), spun off in 2014 from [Agilent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agilent "Agilent"),[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-89) which was itself spun off from [HP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard") in 1999 as an independent, publicly traded company,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-90) has its [oscilloscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscilloscope "Oscilloscope") research and development division based in Colorado Springs. [Intel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intel "Intel") had 250 employees in 2009 but has ceased operations.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-91) The Intel facility is now used for the centralized unemployment offices, social services, El Paso county offices, and a bitcoin mining facility.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-92)[Microchip Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microchip_Technology "Microchip Technology") (formerly [Atmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmel "Atmel")), is a chip fabrication organization.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-93) The [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") facility was sold to Sanmina-SCI in 1996.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Tourism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Tourism")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PikesPeakFromUCCS.jpg/250px-PikesPeakFromUCCS.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PikesPeakFromUCCS.jpg)

[Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak"), the easternmost "[fourteener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteener "Fourteener")" in the United States

Almost immediately following the arrival of railroads beginning in 1871, the city's location at the base of [Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak") and the [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") made it a popular tourism destination. Tourism is the third largest employer in the Pikes Peak region, accounting for more than 16,000 jobs.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-94) In 2018, 23 million day and overnight visitors came to the area, contributing $2.4 billion in revenue.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-95)

### Marijuana

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Marijuana")]

Main article: [Colorado Amendment 64 §Local option](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Amendment_64#Local_option "Colorado Amendment 64")

Although Colorado voters approved [Colorado Amendment 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Amendment_64 "Colorado Amendment 64"), a constitutional amendment in 2012 legalizing retail sales of marijuana for recreational purposes, the Colorado Springs city council voted not to permit retail shops in the city, as was allowed in the amendment.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-136) Medical marijuana outlets continue to operate in Colorado Springs.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-137) In 2015, there were 91 medical marijuana clinics in the city, which reported sales of $59.6 million in 2014, up 11 percent from the previous year but without [recreational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_policy_of_Colorado#Recreational_marijuana "Cannabis policy of Colorado") marijuana shops.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-138) On April 26, 2016, Colorado Springs city council decided to extend the current six-month moratorium to eighteen months with no new licenses to be granted until May 2017. A scholarly paper suggested the city would give up $25.4 million in tax revenue and fees if the city continued to thwart the industry from opening within the city limits.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-139)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-140) As of March 1, 2018, there were 131 medical marijuana centers and no recreational cannabis stores.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-141) In November 2024 a referendum vote allowed existing medical marijuana dispensaries to obtain recreational marijuana sales licenses, and recreational sales began in April 2025.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-142)

### In popular culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: In popular culture")]

Colorado Springs has been the subject of or setting for many books, films and television shows, and is a frequent backdrop for political thrillers and military-themed stories because of its many military installations and vital importance to the United States' continental defense. Notable television series using the city as a setting include _[Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr.\_Quinn,\_Medicine\_Woman "Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman")_, _[Homicide Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homicide\_Hunter "Homicide Hunter")_ and the _[Stargate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate "Stargate")_ series _[Stargate SG-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate\_SG-1 "Stargate SG-1")_, as well as the films _[WarGames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WarGames "WarGames")_, _[The Prestige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Prestige "The Prestige")_, and _[BlacKkKlansman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlacKkKlansman "BlacKkKlansman")_.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-143)

In a North Korean propaganda video released in April 2013, Colorado Springs was singled out as one of four targets for a missile strike. The video failed to pinpoint Colorado Springs on the map, instead showing a spot somewhere in Louisiana.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-144)

### Trails

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Trails")]

Three trails, the New Santa Fe Regional Trail, [Pikes Peak Greenway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak_Greenway "Pikes Peak Greenway") and Fountain Creek Regional Trail, form a continuous path from [Palmer Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmer_Lake,_Colorado "Palmer Lake, Colorado"), through Colorado Springs, to [Fountain, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain,_Colorado "Fountain, Colorado"). The majority of the trail between Palmer Lake and Fountain is a soft surface breeze gravel trail. A major segment of the trail within the Colorado Springs city limits is paved. The trails, except [Monument Valley Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_Valley_Park "Monument Valley Park") trails, may be used for equestrian traffic. Motorized vehicles are not allowed on the trails. Many of the trails are interconnected, having main spine trails, like the Pikes Peak Greenway, that lead to secondary trails.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-170)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-PPG_TRail-171)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-PPG_TRail_Map-172)

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Government")]

See also: [List of mayors of Colorado Springs, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "List of mayors of Colorado Springs, Colorado")

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Colorado_Springs%2C_Colorado_city_hall.jpg/250px-Colorado_Springs%2C_Colorado_city_hall.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colorado_Springs,_Colorado_city_hall.jpg)

[Colorado Springs City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_City_Hall "Colorado Springs City Hall")

On November 2, 2010, Colorado Springs voters adopted a council-[strong mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strong_mayor "Strong mayor") form of government. The City of Colorado Springs transitioned to the new system of government in 2011. Under the council-strong mayor system of government, the mayor is the chief executive and the city council is the legislative branch. The mayor is a full-time elected position and not a member of the council. The council has nine members, six of whom represent one of six equally populated districts each. The remaining three members are elected at-large.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-173)

[Colorado Springs City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_City_Hall "Colorado Springs City Hall") was built from 1902 to 1904 on land donated by [W. S. Stratton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._S._Stratton "W. S. Stratton").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-174)

### City Council

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: City Council")]

The Colorado Springs City Council is the legislative branch that governs the City of [Colorado Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso_County,_Colorado "El Paso County, Colorado"). It has 3 members elected by the district [at-large](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-large "At-large"), with a combined total of 9 official members elected [at-large](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-large "At-large"), with a total 6 of the elected officials representing equally-populated quadrants. The current City Council president, Lynnette Crow-Iverson, was sworn in on April 14, 2025.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-175)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-176)

### Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Politics")]

In 2017, Caleb Hannan wrote in _[Politico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politico\_(magazine) "Politico (magazine)")_ that Colorado Springs was "staunchly Republican", "a right-wing counterweight to liberal [Boulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulder,_Colorado "Boulder, Colorado")", and that a study ranked it "the fourth most conservative city in America".[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Hannan-177) In 2016, Hannan wrote that downtown Colorado Springs had a different political vibe from the overall area's and that there were "superficial signs of changing demographics".[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Hannan-177) However, since 2020, Colorado Springs has continued to shift towards the political center. In 2022, Governor [Jared Polis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jared_Polis "Jared Polis") won the city in his [bid for reelection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Colorado_gubernatorial_election "2022 Colorado gubernatorial election").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-178) In the [2023 mayoral election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Colorado_Springs_mayoral_election "2023 Colorado Springs mayoral election"), independent candidate [Yemi Mobolade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemi_Mobolade "Yemi Mobolade") handily won the race and became the first elected non-Republican mayor of the city.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-179)

**Colorado Springs** is a [home rule city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Colorado#Home_rule_municipality "List of municipalities in Colorado") that is the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of and the most populous city in [El Paso County, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso_County,_Colorado "El Paso County, Colorado"), United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-COMun-1) The city had a population of 478,961 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), a 15.02% increase since [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020_Census-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020Pop-11) Colorado Springs is the [second-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Colorado "List of municipalities in Colorado") and [most extensive city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_area "List of United States cities by area") by area in the state of Colorado, and the [40th-most-populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population "List of United States cities by population") in the United States.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-PopEstCities-12) It is the principal city of the [Colorado Springs metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_metropolitan_area "Colorado Springs metropolitan area"), which had 755,105 residents in 2020, and the second-most prominent city of the [Front Range Urban Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range_Urban_Corridor "Front Range Urban Corridor"). It is located in east-central Colorado on [Fountain Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain_Creek_(Arkansas_River_tributary) "Fountain Creek (Arkansas River tributary)"), 70 miles (113 km) south of [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver").

At 6,035 feet (1,839 m),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-gnis-5) the city stands over 1 mile (1.6 km) above sea level. It is near the base of [Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak"), which rises 14,115 feet (4,302.31 m) above sea level on the eastern edge of the [Southern Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rocky_Mountains "Southern Rocky Mountains").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Colorado Springs, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "History of Colorado Springs, Colorado")

For a chronological guide, see [Timeline of Colorado Springs, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "Timeline of Colorado Springs, Colorado").

The [Ute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ute_people "Ute people"), [Arapaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arapaho "Arapaho") and [Cheyenne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne "Cheyenne") peoples were the first recorded inhabiting the area which would become Colorado Springs.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-13) Part of the territory included in the United States' 1803 [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase"), the current city area was designated part of the 1854 [Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Territory "Kansas Territory"). In 1859, after the first local settlement was established, it became part of the [Jefferson Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Territory "Jefferson Territory") on October 24 and of [El Paso County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso_County,_Colorado "El Paso County, Colorado") on November 28. [Colorado City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Colorado_City "Old Colorado City") at the [Front Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range "Front Range") confluence of Fountain and Camp creeks was "formally organized on August 13, 1859"[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-14) during the [Pikes Peak Gold Rush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak_Gold_Rush "Pikes Peak Gold Rush"). The [Colorado City, Kansas Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_City,_Kansas_Territory "Colorado City, Kansas Territory"), post office operated from March 24, 1860, until it closed as the Colorado City, Colorado, post office on June 30, 1917.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-CPO-15) Colorado City served as the capital of the [Colorado Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Territory "Colorado Territory") from November 5, 1861, until August 14, 1862, when the capital was moved to [Golden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden,_Colorado "Golden, Colorado").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-16)

In 1871 the [Colorado Springs Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Company "Colorado Springs Company") laid out the towns of La Font (later called [Manitou Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitou_Springs,_Colorado "Manitou Springs, Colorado")) and **Fountain Colony**, upstream and downstream respectively, of Colorado City.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Harrison-17) Later that year, the Fountain Colony was renamed Colorado Springs.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-18) The Colorado Springs, Colorado Territory, post office opened on December 1, 1871.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-CPO-15) The El Paso County seat shifted from Colorado City in 1873 to the Town of Colorado Springs.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Capace-19) So many immigrants from England had settled in Colorado Springs by the early 1870s that Colorado Springs was locally referred to as "Little London".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-20) The town of Colorado Springs was incorporated on June 19, 1886.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-COMun-1)

A second period of annexations occurred during 1889–90, which included Seavey's Addition, West Colorado Springs, East End, and another [North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_North_End_Historic_District_(Colorado_Springs,_Colorado) "Old North End Historic District (Colorado Springs, Colorado)") addition.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-AnnexXLS1990-21) In 1891 the Broadmoor Land Company built the [Broadmoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadmoor,_Colorado "Broadmoor, Colorado") suburb, which included the [Broadmoor Casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadmoor_Casino "Broadmoor Casino"), and by December 12, 1895, the city had "four Mining Exchanges and 275 mining brokers."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-22) By 1898, the city was designated into quadrants by the north-south Cascade Avenue and the east-west Washington/Pikes Peak avenues.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Directory1898-23):10

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Nikola_Tesla%2C_with_his_equipment_Wellcome_M0014782_-_restoration2.jpg/250px-Nikola_Tesla%2C_with_his_equipment_Wellcome_M0014782_-_restoration2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nikola_Tesla,_with_his_equipment_Wellcome_M0014782_-_restoration2.jpg)

[Nikola Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Tesla "Nikola Tesla") sitting in the Colorado Springs Experimental Station with his "[magnifying transmitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnifying_transmitter "Magnifying transmitter")" generating millions of volts

From 1899 to 1901 [Tesla Experimental Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Experimental_Station "Tesla Experimental Station") operated on Knob Hill,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-24) and aircraft flights to the Broadmoor's neighboring fields began in 1919.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NRHPairport-25)[Alexander Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nichols_Field_(Colorado) "Nichols Field (Colorado)") north of the city opened in 1925, and in 1927 the original [Colorado Springs Municipal Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Municipal_Airport "Colorado Springs Municipal Airport") land was purchased east of the city.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NRHPairport-25)

The city's military presence began during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), beginning with Camp Carson (now the 135,000-acre [Fort Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Carson "Fort Carson") base) that was established in 1941.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26) During the war, the [United States Army Air Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces "United States Army Air Forces") leased land adjacent to the municipal airfield, naming it [Peterson Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Field "Peterson Field") in December 1942.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Prinzo-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Directory1916-28)

In November 1950, [Ent Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ent_Air_Force_Base "Ent Air Force Base") was selected as the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") headquarters for [Air Defense Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Defense_Command "Air Defense Command") (ADC). The former WWII Army Air Base, Peterson Field, which had been inactivated at the end of the war, was re-opened in 1951 as a [U.S. Air Force base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Air_Force_Base "Peterson Air Force Base").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-29)[North American Aerospace Defense Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Aerospace_Defense_Command "North American Aerospace Defense Command") (NORAD) was established as a hardened command and control center within the [Cheyenne Mountain Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Mountain_Complex "Cheyenne Mountain Complex") during the Cold War.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30)

Between 1965 and 1968, the [University of Colorado Colorado Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Colorado_Colorado_Springs "University of Colorado Colorado Springs"), [Pikes Peak State College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak_State_College "Pikes Peak State College") and [Colorado Technical University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Technical_University "Colorado Technical University") were established in or near the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Hellmann-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-32) In 1977 most of the former Ent AFB became a [US Olympic training center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Olympic_Training_Center "United States Olympic Training Center"). The [Libertarian Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)") was founded within the city in the 1970s.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-33)

On October 1, 1981, the Broadmoor Addition,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-AnnexXLS1990-21) Cheyenne Canon, [Ivywild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivywild,_Colorado "Ivywild, Colorado"), Skyway, and Stratton Meadows were annexed after the [Colorado Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Supreme_Court "Colorado Supreme Court") "overturned a district court decision that voided the [annexation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation "Annexation")". Further annexations expanding the city include the Nielson Addition and Vineyard Commerce Park Annexation in September 2008.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-AnnexXLS1990-21)

On June 23, 2012, the [Waldo Canyon fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waldo_Canyon_fire "Waldo Canyon fire") began 4 miles (6.4 km) northwest of the city.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-34) The fire ended up destroying 347 homes and killing two people in the city, causing the evacuation of 32,000 residents.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-35) At the time the fire was the most destructive in state history until it was surpassed by the [Black Forest Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Forest_Fire "Black Forest Fire") the following year.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-36)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Colorado_Springs_CO.jpg/250px-Colorado_Springs_CO.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Colorado_Springs_CO.jpg)

View of Colorado Springs and [Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak") from the eastern plains

The city lies in a [semi-arid Steppe region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains"),[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-skybrary.aero-37) with the [Southern Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Rocky_Mountains "Southern Rocky Mountains") to the west, the [Palmer Divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmer_Divide "Palmer Divide") to the north, [high plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains") further east, and high desert lands to the south when leaving [Fountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain,_Colorado "Fountain, Colorado") and approaching [Pueblo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo,_Colorado "Pueblo, Colorado").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-SpringsGovInfo-38) Colorado Springs is 69 miles (111 km) or at best one hour and five minutes south of Denver by car using [I-25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_25_in_Colorado "Interstate 25 in Colorado").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-39)

Colorado Springs has the [greatest total area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_area "List of United States cities by area") of any municipality in Colorado. During the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the city had a total area of 195.761 square miles (507.019 km 2) including 0.362 square miles (0.937 km 2) of water.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020_Census-9)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Climate")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/ISS067-E-170859_Colorado_Springs_through_the_clouds.jpg/250px-ISS067-E-170859_Colorado_Springs_through_the_clouds.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ISS067-E-170859_Colorado_Springs_through_the_clouds.jpg)

View of the city through the clouds on July 1, 2022, taken from the International Space Station with north oriented towards the left

Colorado Springs has a cooler, dry-winter [monsoon influenced continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_climate "Continental climate") ([Köppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_Dwa_/_Cwa_), and its location just east of the Rocky Mountains affords it the rapid warming influence from [chinook winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_winds "Chinook winds") during winter but also subjects it to drastic day-to-day variability in weather conditions.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-40) The city has abundant sunshine year-round, averaging 243 sunny days per year,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-42) and receives approximately 16.5 inches (419 mm) of annual [precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology) "Precipitation (meteorology)"). Due to unusually low precipitation for several years after flooding in 1999, Colorado Springs enacted lawn water restrictions in 2002. These were lifted in 2005[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-SpringsGovInfo-38) but permanently reinstated in December 2019.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-43)

Colorado Springs is one of the most active lightning strike areas in the United States.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-skybrary.aero-37) This natural phenomenon led [Nikola Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Tesla "Nikola Tesla") to select Colorado Springs as the preferred location to build his lab and study electricity.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-44)

#### Seasonal climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Seasonal climate")]

December is typically the coldest month, averaging 30.8°F (−0.7°C). Historically, January had been the coldest month, but, in recent years, December has had both lower daily maxima and minima.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-45) Typically, there are 5.2 nights with sub-0°F (−18°C) lows and 23.6 days where the high does not rise above freezing.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NOAA-46)

Snowfall is usually moderate and remains on the ground briefly because of direct sun, with the city receiving 38 inches (97 cm) per season, although the mountains to the west often receive in excess of triple that amount; March is the snowiest month in the region, both by total accumulation and number of days with measurable snowfall. In addition, 8 of the top 10 heaviest 24-hour snowfalls have occurred from March to May.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NOAA-46) Summers are warm, with July, the warmest month, averaging 70.9°F (21.6°C), and 18 days of 90°F (32°C)+ highs annually. Due to the high elevation and aridity, nights are usually relatively cool and rarely does the low remain above 70°F (21°C).[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NOAA-46) Dry weather generally prevails, but brief afternoon thunderstorms are common, especially in July and August when the city receives the majority of its annual rainfall, due to the [North American monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_monsoon "North American monsoon").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-47)

The first autumn freeze and the last freeze in the spring, on average, occur on October 2 and May 6, respectively; the average window for measurable snowfall (≥0.1 in or 0.25 cm) is October 21 through April 25. Extreme temperatures range from 101°F (38°C) on [June 26, 2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_North_American_heat_wave "2012 North American heat wave"), and most recently on June 21, 2016, down to −27°F (−33°C) on February 1, 1951, and December 9, 1919.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-48)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the population of the city of Colorado Springs was 478,961 ([40th most populous U.S. city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population "List of United States cities by population")), the population of the [Colorado Springs Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs_Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "Colorado Springs Metropolitan Statistical Area") was 755,105 ([79th most populous MSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_metropolitan_area "United States metropolitan area")), and the population of the [Front Range Urban Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_Range_Urban_Corridor "Front Range Urban Corridor") was 5,055,344.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-2020_Census-9)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [2010 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-59) 78.8% of the population of the city was [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_people "White people") (non-Hispanic Whites were 70.7% of the population,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-60) compared with 86.6% in 1970[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-61)), 16.1% [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans") of any race (compared with 7.4% in 1970), 6.3% [Black or African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American "African American"), 3.0% Asian, 1.0% descended from [indigenous peoples of the Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas"), 0.3% descended from [indigenous Hawaiians and other Pacific islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_American "Pacific Islander American"), 5.5% of some other race, and 5.1% of [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_American "Multiracial American"). [Mexican Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_American "Mexican American") made up 14.6% of the city's population, compared with 9.1% in 1990. The median age in the city was 35 years.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-62)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-64)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Economy")]

Colorado Springs's economy is driven primarily by the military, the high-tech industry, and tourism, in that order. The city is experiencing slight growth in the service sectors. As of April 2025, the unemployment rate in Colorado Springs was 4.6%.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-65) The state's unemployment rate was 4.8% compared to 4.2% for the nation.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-66)

### Military

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Military")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/PetersonAFB.jpg/250px-PetersonAFB.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PetersonAFB.jpg)

[United States Space Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Space_Force "United States Space Force")–[Peterson Space Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Space_Force_Base "Peterson Space Force Base") Building 1

As of 2021[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit), there are nearly 45,000 active-duty troops in the Colorado Springs area. There are more than 100,000 veterans and thousands of reservists.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26) The military and defense contractors supply more than 40% of the Pikes Peak region's economy.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26)

Colorado Springs is home to the [Peterson Space Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peterson_Space_Force_Base "Peterson Space Force Base"), [Schriever Space Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schriever_Space_Force_Base "Schriever Space Force Base"), [Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Mountain_Space_Force_Station "Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station"), U.S. Space Command, and Space Operations Command—the largest contingent of space service military installations, responsible for intelligence gathering, space operations, and cyber missions.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67)

Peterson Space Force Base is responsible for the [North American Aerospace Defense Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Aerospace_Defense_Command "North American Aerospace Defense Command") (NORAD) and the [United States Northern Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Northern_Command "United States Northern Command") (USNORTHCOM) headquarters,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30) Space Operations Command, and Space Deltas 2, 3, and 7.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67) Located at Peterson is the 302nd Airlift Wing, an Air Force Reserve unit, that transports passengers and cargo and fights wildfires.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67)

Schriever Space Force Base is responsible for Joint Task Force-Space Defense and Space Deltas [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Delta_6 "Space Delta 6"), 8, and 9.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Bitton-67) The NORAD and USNORTHCOM Alternate Command Center is located at the [Cheyenne Mountain Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne_Mountain_Complex "Cheyenne Mountain Complex").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30) Within the mountain complex, the Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station has been operated by [Space Operations Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Operations_Command "Space Operations Command").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-NORAD-30) On January 13, 2021, the Air Force announced a new permanent home for Space Command, moving it from Colorado Springs to Huntsville, Alabama in 2026, but the decision could be reversed by Congress.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-68)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-72)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/President_Richard_Nixon_Gives_a_Commencement_Ceremony_Speech_at_Air_Force_Academy_in_Colorado_Springs_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-President_Richard_Nixon_Gives_a_Commencement_Ceremony_Speech_at_Air_Force_Academy_in_Colorado_Springs_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Richard_Nixon_Gives_a_Commencement_Ceremony_Speech_at_Air_Force_Academy_in_Colorado_Springs_(cropped).jpg)

President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") gives a commencement ceremony speech at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, June 4, 1969.

Army divisions are trained and stationed at [Fort Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Carson "Fort Carson"). The [United States Air Force Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force_Academy "United States Air Force Academy") was established after World War II on land donated by the City of Colorado Springs.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-Roeder-26)

### Defense industry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Defense industry")]

The defense industry forms a significant part of the Colorado Springs economy, with some of the city's largest employers being defense contractors.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-73) Some defense corporations have left or downsized city campuses, but slight growth has been recorded. Significant defense corporations in the city include [Northrop Grumman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northrop_Grumman "Northrop Grumman"), [Boeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing "Boeing"), [General Dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics "General Dynamics"), [L3Harris Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L3Harris_Technologies "L3Harris Technologies"), [SAIC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_Applications_International_Corporation "Science Applications International Corporation"), [ITT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITT_Corporation "ITT Corporation"), [Lockheed Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_Martin "Lockheed Martin"), and Bluestaq.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-74)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-75)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-76)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-77) The [Space Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Foundation "Space Foundation") is based in Colorado Springs.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-78)

### High-tech industry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: High-tech industry")]

A large percentage of Colorado Springs's economy is still based on manufacturing [high-tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-tech "High-tech") and complex electronic equipment. The high-tech sector in the Colorado Springs area has decreased its overall presence from 2000 to 2006 (from around 21,000 to around 8,000), with notable reductions in information technology and complex electronic equipment.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-79) Current trends project the high-tech employment ratio will continue to decrease.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-autogenerated1-80)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-81)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-82)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-83)[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_]

High-tech corporations offering fibre-optics to the premises connections within the city include: [Lumen Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumen_Technologies "Lumen Technologies"), [Comcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comcast "Comcast") and other providers as of 2023.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-84)[Hewlett-Packard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard") still has some sales, support, and [SAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storage_area_network "Storage area network") storage engineering center for the computer industry.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-85)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-86)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-87)[Storage Networking Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storage_Networking_Industry_Association "Storage Networking Industry Association") is the home of the SNIA Technology Center.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-88)[Keysight Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keysight_Technologies "Keysight Technologies"), spun off in 2014 from [Agilent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agilent "Agilent"),[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-89) which was itself spun off from [HP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard") in 1999 as an independent, publicly traded company,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-90) has its [oscilloscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscilloscope "Oscilloscope") research and development division based in Colorado Springs. [Intel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intel "Intel") had 250 employees in 2009 but has ceased operations.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-91) The Intel facility is now used for the centralized unemployment offices, social services, El Paso county offices, and a bitcoin mining facility.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-92)[Microchip Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microchip_Technology "Microchip Technology") (formerly [Atmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmel "Atmel")), is a chip fabrication organization.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-93) The [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") facility was sold to Sanmina-SCI in 1996.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Arts and culture

### Tourism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Colorado_Springs,_Colorado&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Tourism")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PikesPeakFromUCCS.jpg/250px-PikesPeakFromUCCS.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PikesPeakFromUCCS.jpg)

[Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak"), the easternmost "[fourteener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteener "Fourteener")" in the United States

Almost immediately following the arrival of railroads beginning in 1871, the city's location at the base of [Pikes Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pikes_Peak "Pikes Peak") and the [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") made it a popular tourism destination. Tourism is the third largest employer in the Pikes Peak region, accounting for more than 16,000 jobs.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-94) In 2018, 23 million day and overnight visitors came to the area, contributing $2.4 billion in revenue.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs#cite_note-95)
